newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - May 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - May 1.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Thursday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* The government reported that the U.S. economy grew 5.6 percent on an annual basis in the first quarter, helped by strong consumer spending, warm weather and inventory buildup.
* The Justice Department announced a probe into possible bid rigging during airwave auctions recently held by the Federal Communications Commission for wireless phone licenses.
* The FCC is getting ready to overhaul U.S. phone charges in an attempt to make telephone companies compete for residential customers as well as business customers.
* The United Auto Workers disputes with General Motors could grow, if new strikes at plants cause parts shortages which would force the closure of much of the company's North American operations.
* People close to the matter say mutual-fund company Scudder is being shopped to U.S. and foreign financial firms, in a deal which could be worth $1 billion to $1.5 billion.
* Fidelity Investments appointed a new three-member group to oversee its equity mutual funds.
* Interpublic is seen announcing an agreement to take a stake in Nicholson New York, a firm which helps company plan Internet strategies.
* Time Warner said it intended to shut its interactive-television network in Orlando, Fla.
* There is increased Federal Trade Commission scrutiny of tobacco company ads even though a federal judge ruled the U.S. Food and Drug Administration did not have authority to regulate them.
* Aeroflot and Boeing signed a deal for the Russian carrier to buy 10 Boeing 737-400 passenger jets.
* Giddings & Lewis said it wanted to explore other strategic alternatives to Harnischfeger's hostile $19 per share takeover bid.
* Columbia/HCA posted a 15 percent increase in quarterly profits despite slower growth in same-hospital inpatient admissions, it said.
* ValuJet, which is still trying to recover from a fatal plane crash in Florida about one year ago, reported a quarterly loss which was wider than expected.

* Heard on the Street: Is Sanford Weill about to leave the bargain basement to make a full-price acquisition? That's the question making the rounds as the legendary deal maker and cost cutter scourts for acquisition possibilities for Travelers Group .

* Credit markets: Bond prices rose for the third consecutive session on renewed investor optimism, extending a rally that has helped Treasury securities erase the heavy losses triggered by the March 25 interest rate increase.
